summary: Atomic sequencing & per-tool idempotency for concurrent async tool chains in Python SDK
description:
Issue summary:
Customer runs an async orchestration (Python asyncio) that issues multiple function/tool calls in a logical chain. Each tool performs an external side-effect (HTTP POST to downstream service). When their client retries certain requests concurrently (client-side backoff/backpressure), downstream endpoints occasionally receive duplicate side-effects out of order. Customer wants guidance for SDK patterns to ensure atomic sequencing or at-most-once semantics for chained tool calls while still using streaming/batched requests to reduce token cost.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream posts occasionally leading to double-recording of events in customer's system (financial data).
- Ordering violations observed when two retries overlap; leads to state inconsistency.

Environment:
- Python SDK (asyncio, version 2.8.1)
- Dedicated capacity (us-east), autoscaled pool with burst enabled
- Using streaming responses + per-tool function calling via the SDK
- Network path includes an edge-side reverse proxy + internal API gateway

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start orchestration that calls Tool A -> Tool B -> Tool C as sequence. Each tool triggers a webhook POST to an internal endpoint.
2) Introduce transient 500s on the gateway for 1–2s to force SDK retry/backoff paths.
3) SDK retries the streaming segment and replays the same tool-call events; due to concurrent retry, two active attempts overlap.
4) Downstream webhook receives two POSTs for Tool B with slightly different timestamps and out-of-order relative to Tool A/C.

Expected behavior:
- Either a single side-effect per logical tool invocation (at-most-once) or clear ordering guarantees so that downstream can deterministically apply updates.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate POSTs for the same logical tool action in ~0.3% of runs under induced transient failures.
- Sometimes order of POSTs is shuffled when replay and live attempt interleave.

comments: 2026-03-10T09:08:12Z - Support (Aisha): Triage assigned. Reproduced locally with our transient-failure test harness against dedicated pool (small traffic). Adding Diego from infra to investigate routing/retry interactions.

2026-03-11T11:42:07Z - Diego Morales (Infra): Observed overlapping inflight attempts in SDK logs. The SDK replays tool events during reconnect without annotating a replay-vs-first-delivery flag. Recommend per-action idempotency keys from client side to help downstream dedupe.

2026-03-12T15:20:30Z - Customer (Ferrosa Health): We're already generating UUIDs per logical action but duplicates still arrive because both attempts use same UUID and race ordering causes downstream to apply timestamps out-of-order. Need guidance on both dedupe and ordering guarantees we can rely on from Redwood API/SDK.

2026-03-13T08:05:02Z - Support (Aisha): Requested exact SDK trace and a minimal repro script. Suggested short-term workaround: implement confirm-token handshake (client gets a tool-exec-ack from downstream and pauses replay until ack) or make downstream idempotent+sequence-aware (accept sequence numbers).
investigation: Reproduced with dedicated pool using customer's repro harness. When reconnect happens, SDK resends in-flight tool events with identical idempotency_uuid (good), but there is no sequencing enforcement on server side when two attempts arrive close together.

Serving runtime accepts events and forwards to routing which batches / routes to downstream webhook via customer's configured callback URL. Router does not currently serialize replays by idempotency key across concurrent connections; it is opportunistic (best-effort).
Edge proxy sometimes rewrites chunk boundaries causing two distinct connection attempts to appear nearly simultaneous to the router, increasing chance of race.
resolution: - Add a monotonic sequence number per logical chain and attach both sequence and idempotency_uuid to each tool invocation. Downstream should discard or reorder based on sequence if it sees a lower/higher number and keep last-applied sequence per entity.

- Implement a confirm-ack pattern: after the tool triggers downstream POST, downstream returns a confirmation token that client records; client will suppress replays if token present. This is useful when downstream can return durable acknowledgment quickly.
- Temporarily increase SDK reconnect backoff (configurable in Python SDK via ClientConfig.stream_backoff_base) to reduce overlap during flakey gateway periods.

- ENG-12547 (internal): Add 'replay-flag' metadata on server-ack so SDK can differentiate replay vs fresh delivery. This will allow client-side logic to gate side-effects when it knows an event is being replayed.

- INFRA-9853 (internal): Investigate router serialization option for per-idempotency-key dedupe at ingress for dedicated pools (configurable, opt-in) — avoids races by queuing same-key deliveries briefly.
Follow-up: Customer agreed to implement sequence numbers + confirm-ack and to test under a 48-hour window. We scheduled a sync on 2026-03-15 to validate results.
resolution_notes: Customer accepted short-term guidance (sequence numbers + confirm-ack). Product tickets created for optional server-side replay metadata and ingress dedupe. Pending follow-up sync and validation on 2026-03-15.
